name: olai-plugin-kolu
//name: UNSCOPED, and that is the prefix doing its job. `@olai/*` is the scope for the packages that ARE olai; a tenant is olai's judgement about somebody else's appliance, which is the closest thing in this tree to a plugin somebody outside it would write — and the day one arrives it is `olai-plugin-<something>`, resolved and named exactly like this one, with nothing about the two in here special. The directory carries the same word (`packages/plugins/olai-plugin-kolu`), which is this repo's one naming law: a directory is its package's name, and `packages/plugin-api/src/fence.test.ts` reads the tree by it.
//exports: Five entries, and the first three are DISJOINT graphs — it is `@olai/kolu-client`'s own split one floor down, grown a door. `./wire` is the member declarations and nothing else, reached through `@olai/plugin-api/wire`: everything that composes or reads the surface pulls it in statically, so it may carry no UI runtime (a server reads it) and no padi (a browser will). The root is the MANIFEST — the dressing, the chrome and the tab's own mount — and that is where this plugin's browser faces hang, which is `./src/appliance/` and therefore SolidJS and an emulator. `./server` is EVERYTHING THAT RUNS IN A SERVER PROCESS: the runtime half (the `koluHalf` call, the two vault walks, and the deps a composition root hands `implementSurfaces`) and the PROBE beside it — whether this host is running kolu, asked per chat session, plus the five English sentences saying why not. It is its own door for two reasons that are the same reason twice: a server reaching the runtime half through the manifest would pull a UI runtime onto the graph of a process that renders nothing, and a browser reaching the probe through it would pull `node:child_process` and kolu's whole detect surface into the tab — which is the hazard `@olai/kolu-client/wire`'s own fence was written for one floor down, from each side. The last two are the browser half's two contracts with packages that never import it: `./testids` is NAMES ONLY, so a scenario asserts on this package's own DOM without pulling a component into a suite that has no browser, and `./all.css` is the sheet — the emulator's and the row's chain plus a `@source` at BOTH face directories, because Tailwind emits only what it can SEE and a moved component nothing points at renders with no layout and nothing errors. `@olai/plugin-api` mirrors the three code doors and `packages/plugin-api/src/fence.test.ts` walks each closure. The third product is not a JavaScript export at all: `default.nix` beside this manifest, which reads the pinned kolu's `packages/client/favicon.svg` — the same npins revision the `@kolu/*` sources hydrate from — and writes the mark module `just install` copies into `src/browser/`. No `exports` entry for it, because a derivation is not a door.
//: THE KOLU TENANT — everything that says `kolu`, on this side of the wall. `@olai/kolu-client` is still THE DIAL, in its own package, because it names no olai package at all and the resolver proves that; everything else kolu-shaped is here. `./src/appliance/` is what KOLU renders (the Dock row a `terminal` property wears, the live pane, the fleet a tab holds once, the words the readout says) and was `@olai/kolu-ui` until the appliance fold; `./src/browser/` is what OLAI says about kolu in olai's own chrome; the rest is the judgement — what an absent padi MEANS, which vault file is kolu's, which property kind wears the terminal door — which used to be spread across `@olai/chat`, `@olai/server` and `@olai/web` under kolu-shaped filenames in general packages.
//devDependencies: @types/node is for the `ChildProcess` type `probe.ts` names — `@kolu/detect`'s probe takes Node's own — and for the fixture executables `probe.test.ts` writes. It came with the probe from `@olai/chat`, which is where that same line used to sit.
//dependencies: The dial, the vault's own vocabulary, SolidJS and the emulator. `@olai/kolu-client` is the one olai package this tenant reaches and it is reached through `./wire` and `./detect` as well as its root — the dial stayed a package of its own when `@olai/kolu-ui` folded in here, because a manifest that names no `@olai/*` is a wall the resolver keeps and a directory is not (the appliance fold's own ruling, and `packages/plugin-api/src/fence.test.ts`'s header says what a package wall proves that a sweep has to be written to). `@olai/format` is here because the three vault walks are — and `src/faces.test.ts` is what keeps it OUT of `src/appliance/`, which is the wall `@olai/kolu-ui`'s own manifest used to keep by not declaring it; it — `claimants.ts`, `config.ts` and `doorbell.ts` read outline records, which is precisely why they may not live in `@olai/kolu-client` (whose interfaces are parametric in the node type so a compiler holds it to that) and why they no longer live in `@olai/server` (a general package with an appliance in a filename). It is a devDependency nowhere: the walks are product. `solid-js` is a runtime dependency because this package owns every face kolu wears — the Dock row and the live pane in `./src/appliance/`, the padi pill and the tab's mount in `./src/browser/`. `@xterm/*` came in with the fold and is ordinary npm rather than a hydrated pin: the emulator is this appliance's, and `@olai/web` has no business declaring a terminal renderer. `effect` came in with the fold too and was UNDECLARED until an audit of this round found it: three of the folded files import it (`appliance/props/KoluUi.tsx`, `appliance/props/LivePane.tsx`, `appliance/props/fleet.tsx`), `@olai/kolu-ui` never declared it either, and it resolved only by walking up to the root — a walk-up `bunfig.toml` reserves for the HYDRATED `@kolu/*` sources, not for a first-class runtime import of a member's own code. Every other olai package that imports `effect` declares it; these were the exceptions. `scripts/check-hydrated-deps.sh` now holds this manifest to the pin's version like every other. `@olai/plugin-api` is deliberately ABSENT and its absence is structural rather than tidy: that package imports THIS one, so a dependency back would be a cycle the manifests could not express. The manifest is a plain `as const` and the registry's `satisfies` is what proves it fits — the same structural agreement `@olai/ops` keeps with the surface's `Status`. `@olai/web` is absent for the same reason a hop further out: the pill needs the bar's geometry, the app's popover and its door onto a served file, and every one of those arrives as a VALUE (src/browser/app.ts declares the shapes structurally and argues why) rather than as an import that would be a cycle. `@olai/surface` is absent for the same reason one more hop.
